summary.text: A 78-year-old man with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, vascular epilepsy and acute ischemic stroke was admitted to a nursing home in August 2023. He had right-sided hemiparesis, global aphasia, dysphagia and full dependence for daily activities, and fed through a nasogastric tube with a homemade liquid diet. Admission BMI was 18.8 Kg/m^(2) with an estimated weight of 55.7 Kg.

One month after admission chronic bronchitis was diagnosed with dyspnea, wheezing and productive cough, and a PEG was placed to improve nutritional status while keeping the homemade liquid diet. A multidisciplinary team chose the PEG over the nasogastric tube for long-term feeding. Calf circumference fell below 31 cm by February 2024, confirming sarcopenia, and the authors classified moderate malnutrition and mild anemia.

Six months after PEG placement a normocaloric enteric formula was added to the diet. Weight loss continued, so a main course was added and later removed because of gastric contents before meals and possible gastric stasis. A hypercaloric enteral formula replaced the normocaloric one for 5 days. In April 2024 diarrhea led to stopping the normocaloric formula and an antidiarrheal diet, after which the diet and formula were reintroduced.

Over the 10-month follow-up the patient gained weight after the diarrhea episodes and in May 2024 had gained 1.5 kg with BMI 16.8 Kg/m^(2). The authors describe improved overall nutritional status and improved anthropometric measurements, while laboratory values showed mixed changes.
